references.text: The same Aaron and Moses whom the Lord commanded to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt according to their hosts.
The Lord announces that he will lead his hosts, his people the children of Israel, out of Egypt.
The expression 'on this very day' is used for the day when the Lord led the hosts of Israel out of Egypt.
Parallel verses describing how all the hosts of the Lord went out of Egypt on this very day.
Moses reminds the people of this day when they went out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
Summary of the children of Israel's departure from Egypt under the leadership of Moses and Aaron, arranged according to their hosts.
Israel organized by hosts, which connects to the description of the armies that left.
The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, to be his own possession.
Stephen's speech mentions Moses leading the people out of Egypt with signs and wonders.
Reference to the day when God took hold of the hand of Israel's fathers and led them out of Egypt.
Highlights the connection between the departure from the city and the final deliverance at the Red Sea.
Theological summary confirming God's action in the exodus from Egypt as the foundation for liberation.
Supplementary perspective on the exodus by highlighting the role of the prophet Moses as God's instrument.
The direct continuation that establishes the eternal liturgical significance of the day of departure.
Chronological link showing how material preparations led to the final departure.
Illuminates the same sequence of events by showing the judgment on the persecutors that followed the exodus.
